What Are Workflow Automation Tools? Workflow automation tools add integrations between various apps and services to automate repeated tasks, without human action. You can think of them as digital bridges that connect applications such as Gmail, Slack, and Google Sheets so that the information flows smoothly and workflows remain streamlined. There are such solutions as Zapier and Make.com that help to create clever automated workflows that can save time and minimize mistakes. The solutions Zapier vs Make eliminate such difficulties, reduce the possibility of an error, and make the process faster and allowing teams to focus on strategic work while routine tasks run in the background. What is this Zapier? Zapier is a versatile no-code automation technology that works to connect favorite apps of a company and executes recurrent tasks without any human input. Within the ecosystem of Zapier, any automated workflow is referred to as a Zap, a set of rules, which activate certain actions upon the realization of a predetermined set of circumstances. A Zap consists of two key components: A single trigger: This is an occasion that initiates automation. For example, receiving an email written with the word Request in the subject line . A sequence of actions: here is a linear order of steps which are followed. You are allowed to place filters, conditional paths in order to lead the process. An example is that when the word logistics is mentioned in the request, it can be directed to Marc automatically. Otherwise, the process workflow could trigger a new transaction in the ticketing system of the firm. The amount of actions within a Zap technically limitless although there are key precautions to bear in mind: Each Zap can only has a single trigger .Multiple triggers would need several Zaps Zapier uses linear workflows–a step can never follow more than one path, and once a step has been performed, it cannot be re-added to an alternative branch. Loops, backward or re-entry into previous steps is not supported. Automation Examples with Zapier Lead Management & CRM: When a form (e.g. Typeform) is filled in, Zapier can enrich CRM systems like Salesforce or HubSpot. It can automatically make new contacts, log company information, request legal records, or even send an appointment link using Calendly- all through one trigger. Notifications & Customer Support: Working from an incoming email request, Zapier can create a support ticket in Zendesk or Freshservice, assign to the correct agent by expertise or availability and include contextually-relevant information in the ticket. Automated Email Attachment Backup: Zapier is able to extract email attachments and immediately back them up in Google drive, drop box or one drive without any manual download. Massive library of app integrations and API connections with the world-renowned business tools. Capability of building on lightweight databases and interfaces as well as automated workflows. Key Limitations of Zapier Only linear structure- no branching workflows such as those with backtrack or multi entry points to data. Reduced series of human-in-the-loop automation, in which coordination is necessary. Similarly, to its rival Zapier, it allows companies to link various applications and develop automated procedures without even touching a line of code. Within the Make ecosystem, an automation is known as Scenario. A scenario will begin with a single trigger event after which a number of actions will be associated, this may be augmented with filters, conditions and branching paths to specify data flow. In case you require multiple triggers to a process, you have to come up with multiple scenarios. Make does also support linear automated tasks but it’s particularly known for being better at messing around with longer, more complex multi-step workflows with a higher degree of customization over some of its rivals.
